meta.title: Same Scale, Different Body
meta.disclaimer: Illustrative simulation for education. Not a clinical diagnostic tool.

women.name: Woman A

risk.label: High — hidden visceral fat, low muscle

women.note: This is the 'skinny fat' pattern. After menopause, falling estrogen can push fat into the abdomen and away from the hips even when scale weight barely moves. Visceral fat is metabolically active and inflammatory; low muscle reduces glucose disposal. A low BMI can mask real cardiometabolic risk.

women.name: Woman B

risk.label: Low — protective muscle, little visceral fat

women.note: Higher BMI does not automatically mean higher risk. Muscle supports glucose metabolism, bone density, and balance — all especially important as women age. With low visceral fat and strong muscle, this profile can be metabolically healthier than a lower-BMI, low-muscle body.

women.name: Woman C
women.note: Equal muscle and visceral fat with more subcutaneous fat. Subcutaneous fat is generally less harmful than visceral fat, but the balance here means risk is real and modifiable. The target is not simply a lower number — it is shifting the ratio toward muscle and away from visceral fat.
